summary: A 164 x 83 m (native extent), Z-shaped complex of 5-6 storey wings round courtyards, one BAG pand, built 1941 (BAG) and extended later. 3DBAG LoD2.2 gives 237 wall surfaces and a roof max of 24.8 m. The brief assumed a single 1930s traditionalist block with a carved portal and a crowned corner tower; the panoramas and 3DBAG show a composite of at least four facade types and no tower or carved portal.

findings.reads: dark brick, three storeys of white steel-window ribbons (~14 bays) under a recessed white top ribbon, glazed ground ribbon right, gated vehicle entrance left, round (porthole) windows on the end pier; trees in front

findings.wall: SW, 27 m (panel 3), bearing 247, on the Singelgracht
findings.reads: pinkish stone cladding with square yellow-framed windows (3 rows of ~11), yellow-framed top ribbon, tall yellow-framed glazed bay at ground, stone sculpture group on a bracket, brick quay base; a later wing, not the 1941 brick

findings.wall: SW, 60 m (panel 29), bearing 247, raised ground 8.6 m
findings.reads: white steel-window ribbon wing of two storeys over a brick base, a bridge-like upper wing
1941 brick: sash windows with heavy white stone hoods and sills, chequer brick bands between window rows, barred basement windows

Marnixstraat end block: brick, ribbon windows on the middle floors, glazed ground floor with a stair, flat canopy on one post, small blue POLITIE sign on a bracket, curved glazed top storey under an overhanging roof, a balcony at first floor; 3DBAG has it as a plain box with a chimney

notSupportedByEvidence: carved stone entrance portal with lettering
steep tiled roofs with dormers (3DBAG roofs are mostly low-slope or flat; no panorama sees the roofs)
